calls.head: Who drives the play: the Mammoth
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Mammoth have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Jets near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Mammoth’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Mammoth
calls.body: The Jets’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Mammoth’s power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Jets tonight.

calls.head: The Mammoth will pepper the Jets
calls.body: The Mammoth shoot a lot, but the Jets don’t. Utah is one of the league’s best for shot volume, and Winnipeg is near the bottom. Expect the Mammoth to spend more of the night in the attacking zone.

UTA.head: We leaned Utah’s way (59%), but Winnipeg had other ideas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Vilardi lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: There were five goals in the first period alone. Gabriel Vilardi opened the scoring for the Jets early in the period, but Andrew Peeke tied it up for Utah just over a minute later. Vilardi scored again just over a minute later to put the Jets back ahead 2-1. Lawson Crouse made it 2-2 for Utah just under three minutes later, but that was the last goal the Mammoth would get. Morgan Barron put the Jets ahead for good less than four minutes later, and Vilardi completed his hat trick into the empty net with just seven seconds left.

The Mammoth outshot the Jets 36-15, but the Jets’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Stuart Skinner shook off a shaky start for the Jets, allowing two goals on the first six shots and none on the last 30, and Sebastian Cossa stopped 11 of 14 at the other end.
Mark Scheifele and Mikhail Sergachev picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Jets moved to 12-9-4 and took sixth place in the Central from the Mammoth, who fell to 12-10-3.

items.text: The Mammoth’s Dylan Guenther was back in the lineup after missing six games.
The Mammoth have gone winless in four straight on the road.
The Jets have won eight of their last ten.
The Mammoth were without Nate Schmidt, John Marino, Michael Carcone and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team was missing more at the time.
